author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name, all on one unpaged page reached by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html renders a page listing every specialty the clinic knows, all on that one page with no pagination.
Each specialty is shown by its stored name.
Under each specialty, every veterinarian holding it is listed by full name, first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page.
A veterinarian holding more than one specialty is listed under each specialty they hold (PRD Veterinarian directory edge case 3).
A specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it (edge case 4).
A specialty's name reads as stored in whichever supported language the page is presented (edge case 5).
non_goals: Adding, changing, or removing veterinarians, specialties, or who holds which: NG-2 is unchanged (intake line 1 decision).
A navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty page; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request (intake line 1 decision).
Searching or filtering on the specialty page: the page is a full listing and NG-9 stands.
A machine-readable form of the specialty listing: REQ-VET-002 was withdrawn for having no consumer, and the request asks for a page only.
Any change to the veterinarian directory page (REQ-VET-001).
notes: Boundary check against existing REQs found no contradiction, so no pushback. Open questions are recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions and resolved to the narrowest reading, per the owner's instruction: (1) no order is promised for specialties or for the veterinarians under each, so tests assert membership, not sequence; (2) a specialty no veterinarian holds needs no 'none' marker, only an empty listing; (3) the visible entry point is deferred to a follow-up request. Existing requirements bind the page: REQ-SYS-001 (it carries the standard navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory) and REQ-LANG-002 (its own wording exists in every supported language; specialty and veterinarian names are data, shown as stored). PRD delta: REQ-VET-003 narrative, three Done-when bullets, edge cases 3-5 in the Veterinarian directory group, a Context sentence, the provenance header now exempting requirements marked requested, and three Open Questions. No Non-Goals row changed; docs/ubiquitous-language.md unchanged.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing vet-package patterns with one small adjustment. The page is a new read surface in the vet feature package (ADR feature-package-organization): a package-private SpecialtyController beside VetController, a SpecialtyRepository following the lookup-repository precedent of PetTypeRepository but in VetRepository's minimal marker-Repository shape, and a vets/specialtyList template on the standard layout fragment. The adjustment: every specialty the clinic knows (edge case 4, an unheld specialty) cannot be derived from the veterinarian collection, so specialties are read on their own, and the pairing of each specialty with its holders lives in a pure value object, SpecialtyHolders, not in the controller (architecture-principles Pattern Catalog: Value object, In force; Web controller holds no business rule). No service layer is introduced. Specialty keeps no association back to its holders. Basis: grep over src/main/java (IDE oracle not connected, the weaker basis) resolved VetRepository.findAll() (unpaged, @Cacheable vets), Vet.getSpecialties(), BaseEntity with no equals/hashCode, and CacheConfiguration declaring only the vets cache. docs/system-design.md Contracts now carries REQ-VET-003 on Vet, Specialty, VetRepository and three new rows, plus the invariant that SpecialtyHolders matches holders by specialty identifier.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html (SpecialtyController): binds no request input. The handler declares no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, or @ModelAttribute, so there is no binding target and no persisted type is bound; the lang parameter is consumed by WebConfiguration's LocaleChangeInterceptor, not the handler (security-principles Realization: Mass assignment applies to request-bound types only).

Controller flow: constructor-injected SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository (architecture-principles Design Principle 3); the handler reads specialtyRepository.findAll() and the existing cached vetRepository.findAll(), passes both to SpecialtyHolders.of(specialties, vets), adds the resulting list to the model, and returns view vets/specialtyList. No paging parameter and no Pageable (prd-entry non-goal: pagination).

SpecialtyHolders: public record of one Specialty and its holder List<Vet> (List.copyOf in the compact constructor, architecture-principles Domain Core: defensive copies); public because the Thymeleaf template engine reads its accessors reflectively (Design Principle 5 names that caller). The package-private static factory of(Collection<Specialty>, Collection<Vet>) returns one entry per specialty, holders being the vets whose specialties include that specialty's identifier; it imports no Spring or persistence type.

SpecialtyRepository: package-private interface extending org.springframework.data.repository.Repository<Specialty, Integer> with one @Transactional(readOnly = true) findAll(); not @Cacheable (CacheConfiguration declares only the vets cache).

Template vets/specialtyList.html: fragments/layout :: layout (~{::body}, 'specialties') so the standard navigation renders (REQ-SYS-001); layout.html gains no menu item (intake decision, prd-entry non-goal). Holder full name composed as in vetList.html (firstName + ' ' + lastName); specialty and vet names render with th:text from data, never a message lookup (REQ-LANG-002 note in system-design Contracts).

Messages: reuse existing keys present in every bundle (specialties, vets) for the heading and labels; any new key must land in every messages*.properties bundle, which I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces.

Double, repository boundary (SpecialtyControllerTests): hand-written in-memory doubles implementing SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository (the paged findAll returns a PageImpl over the same list), supplied as beans from a nested @TestConfiguration to @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class). No @MockitoBean: both interfaces are small marker-Repository types, so a hand-written double fits (testing-principles Mocking Policy).

Double, transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned web-test harness (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy). WebConfiguration is a WebMvcConfigurer and is included in the @WebMvcTest slice, so ?lang=<code> drives the real locale switch for theSpecialtyNameShouldReadAsStoredInEverySupportedLanguage across every bundle locale.
No boundary, SpecialtyHoldersTests: plain JUnit over real Vet and Specialty instances built as in VetTests; no doubles.

patterns.description: package-private controller, constructor-injected repository, @GetMapping returning a view name under vets/
marker-Repository interface with @Transactional(readOnly = true) findAll(); SpecialtyRepository mirrors it without @Cacheable
precedent for a repository over a persisted lookup value
layout fragment call, message-key labels, full name composed first name then last name
real entity construction in unit tests
where native-image reflection hints are registered

risks.risk: Specialty instances reached through Vet.getSpecialties() come from VetRepository's cached, separately-transacted load and are distinct objects from those SpecialtyRepository returns; BaseEntity defines no equals, so Set.contains or object equality silently yields an empty holder list under every specialty.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyHolders.of matches by getId() with Objects.equals, never == on boxed Integer ids. SpecialtyHoldersTests pins it with a holder whose Specialty is a distinct instance sharing the identifier, using an identifier above 127. Cites system-design.md Contracts invariant (matching by specialty identifier) and architecture-principles Domain Core (aggregates reference each other by identity).

risks.risk: Grouping vets under specialties inside the controller would add a fresh rule to an entry point, outside the existing recorded deviation.
risks.mitigation: All pairing lives in SpecialtyHolders.of; the controller fetches, delegates, and selects the view. Cites architecture-principles Pattern Catalog Web controller row and Design Principle 4 (Layer respect).

risks.risk: Adding a Specialty-to-Vet association (mappedBy) to reach holders would recurse through the serialized vet collection on /vets and widen the eager-fetch graph.
risks.mitigation: Specialty and Vet mappings stay unchanged. Cites system-design.md Contracts invariant: Specialty maps no association back to its holders.

risks.risk: SpecialtyHolders is the first non-entity type read by a template; in a GraalVM native image the template engine's reflective accessor calls fail without a hint.
risks.mitigation: Register a reflection hint for SpecialtyHolders with public-method invocation in PetClinicRuntimeHints, and assert it with RuntimeHintsPredicates in a plain unit test. Cites system-design.md Overview (native-image build) and the PetClinicRuntimeHints Contracts row.

risks.risk: Hard-coded page text or a key missing from one bundle breaks REQ-LANG-002.
risks.mitigation: Reuse existing keys; any new key goes into every bundle; I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces. Cites system-design.md Contracts note on REQ-LANG-002.
th:text only, never th:utext. Cites security-principles Realization: Cross-site scripting.

risks.risk: Tests asserting order would promise one the PRD leaves open.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository uses plain findAll(); tests assert membership per specialty, not sequence (prd-entry notes, PRD Open Questions).

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. docs/system-design.md writes this dispatch: provenance header sentence marking requested-requirement rows as design; Package Structure vet line; Contracts invariant sentences on Specialty and SpecialtyHolders; REQ-VET-003 added to the Vet, Specialty, VetRepository rows; new rows SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyHolders, SpecialtyController. No ADR: every choice follows the brief's catalog and is contained by this slice. Surface statement (security-principles Realization: Widening the exposed surface): GET /specialties.html exposes specialty names and veterinarian full names, the same data /vets.html already shows, to any caller, within the demonstration baseline; read-only, no management exposure change. Resource bound: the specialty set is a clinic-maintained lookup list with no write path (NG-2), so the unpaged page stays small. The Known Defects row on the machine-readable vet route: its eventual removal must keep VetRepository.findAll(), which now also serves REQ-VET-003 (recorded on the VetRepository Contracts row). The prd-entry test_names go verbatim into SpecialtyControllerTests; SpecialtyHoldersTests carries the identity-matching and unheld-specialty cases at unit level. No ubiquitous-language change: holder follows the recorded Specialty relationship (held by zero or more Veterinarians).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Widening the exposed surface: the one new route, GET /specialties.html (SpecialtyController.java:170 `@GetMapping("/specialties.html")`), is read-only and shows veterinarian names and specialty names. That data is already public unauthenticated through /vets.html and /vets (VetController.java `@GetMapping("/vets.html")`, `@GetMapping({ "/vets" })`), so no new data class is exposed and management-endpoint exposure is unchanged.

Input handling: the handler binds no request input. `grep -n -E '@ModelAttribute|@RequestBody|@RequestParam|@PathVariable'` over SpecialtyController.java, SpecialtyHolders.java, SpecialtyRepository.java and specialtyList.html returns no match, so there is nothing to validate, no mass-assignment target, and no need for an @InitBinder disallow list. The only request parameter that reaches the page is the global `lang` locale switch, which is baseline.

Data access: SpecialtyRepository.findAll() is a Spring Data derived query with no arguments (SpecialtyRepository.java:279 `Collection<Specialty> findAll() throws DataAccessException;`). No query text is concatenated.

XSS: every value in specialtyList.html is rendered through escaping `th:text` (specialtyList.html:305 `th:text="${entry.specialty.name}"`, :308 `th:text="${holder.firstName + ' ' + holder.lastName}"`). A grep for `th:utext` finds nothing in the template. SpecialtyControllerTests uses the stored name `Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery` so that a missing escape would fail the XML parse. The template adds no `__${...}__` preprocessing: the layout's existing `th:href="@{__${link}__}"` (layout.html:31) receives only literal menu links, and the new 'specialties' menu argument is only compared for equality (layout.html:31 `${active==menu ? ...}`).

Unbounded allocation: the page loads every specialty and every vet with no paging, as the PRD requires ("Every specialty appears on the one page, with no paging"). The PRD does not state the size of these tables. Callers cannot grow them: no write path exists in the vet package (`grep -rn -F -e 'save(' src/main/java/.../vet/` and a grep for @Post/@Put/@Delete/@PatchMapping both return nothing). The existing /vets route already returns the full vet collection unpaged, and VetRepository.findAll() is @Cacheable("vets").

Deserialization and native hints: PetClinicRuntimeHints.java:123 grants SpecialtyHolders only `MemberCategory.INVOKE_PUBLIC_METHODS` reflection, so Thymeleaf can read the record's accessors. It adds no Java-serialization hint, unlike the three existing entity hints. SpecialtyHolders defensively copies its holder list (`holders = List.copyOf(holders);`).

Secrets and shell execution: a grep of the diff's added lines for password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential|private.?key returns no match. The only hits for the shell-execution pattern are the `RuntimeHints` class names in PetClinicRuntimeHints.java, which are not process execution. No logging, file I/O, or /tmp use was added. The test's XML parser enables FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING.

Supply chain: `scripts/changeset.sh --name-only` lists no build.gradle, pom.xml, settings.gradle or .properties file, so no dependency changed. The resolved runtimeClasspath shows spring-boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.5. OWASP Dependency-Check is not configured (`grep -n -F dependencyCheck build.gradle` returns nothing), so no NVD match ran in this review.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: The change is additive and stays in one module: three new vet-package types, one new template, a one-line reflection hint in PetClinicRuntimeHints, and doc rows. No sensitive paths, and no existing behavior is edited. The one new unauthenticated route, GET /specialties.html, shows the same names /vets.html already exposes, and layout.html is untouched.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks turned up nothing unexpected. SpecialtyHolders.holds matches with Objects.equals on the ids, not == or instance equality, and it never mutates the cached vet collection because Vet.getSpecialties returns a sorted copy. Vet.specialties is EAGER and Specialty has no lazy fields, so the template is safe with open-in-view=false. Every value renders through th:text. The one theoretical edge, null ids matching each other, cannot arise from persisted rows.

test_adequacy.note: The tests check real outcomes. The controller tests parse the rendered table as strict XML and compare whole specialty-to-holders maps, including an ampersand name that would break the parse if escaping failed. SpecialtyHoldersTests catches the design's main risk by using a separately built specialty with id 1000, beyond the Integer cache. The hint test uses RuntimeHintsPredicates. Minor gap: no test runs SpecialtyRepository.findAll or the page against the real database.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four planned reviewers approved with no findings. But the security-reviewer's file:line citations do not match the files they name: SpecialtyController.java:170 is a 45-line file (the mapping is at line 38), SpecialtyRepository.java:279 is a 37-line file (line 35), PetClinicRuntimeHints.java:123 is actually line 39, and specialtyList.html:305/:308 are actually lines 18 and 21. The quoted snippets exist and the claims hold on my read, but that approval's evidence trail is broken. The Dependency-Check gap is a standing project gap and counts only as context.

scope_deviation.note: The change stays inside the intake decisions and the design-block. It adds no navigation entry or link (layout.html unchanged), no write path, and no paging. The runtime-hint edit and its test are the mitigation the design-block named. The PRD and system-design provenance headers gain one clause each to cover requested requirements, which the prd-entry and design-block both record. There were zero consultations, design revisions, and build retries.

rationale: The code is additive, contained, and well tested, and my read found no behavioral surprise. The one flag is the security-reviewer's approval: none of its file:line citations resolve in the files it names. Spot-check the security claims directly (th:text only, no request binding, the new route) before merging. The rest can be skimmed.
